text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1% today as oil prices climbed on Middle East tensions and geopolitical risk. Brent crude traded above $95 a barrel amid Iran-U.S. escalation, including strikes and disputed mine incidents near the Strait of Hormuz—a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments. Refineries are running at 98% capacity, so higher crude prices directly lift the margins refiners earn on turning oil into gasoline and diesel.

The stock's strong run over the past two weeks (up 7.3%) reflects both tighter supply concerns from geopolitical conflict and robust refining demand, with gasoline and diesel inventories at relatively modest levels. U.S. production moves like Chevron's Venezuela expansion could eventually ease supply pressures, but near-term risk premiums on oil from Mideast instability are supporting refiner economics.
